recent.question: Brock Bowers: 1+ touchdowns
recent.what_happened: Bowers was active and caught 6 of 11 targets for 86 yards. His only touchdown was a 20-yard catch from Kirk Cousins with less than two minutes left, in a game the Raiders lost to the Chiefs. That catch resolved the market YES. ([NBC Sports](https://www.nbcsports.com/fantasy/football/player-news/2026-10-04/brock-bowers-scores-late-td-in-loss-to-chiefs))
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing important. All the forecasts (0.32 to 0.49) and the market (0.345) were close to a fair anytime-TD price for a heavily targeted tight end. The deciding touchdown came on a late garbage-time drive, which no one could have predicted.
recent.lesson: For anytime-TD props on high-target players, a forecast in the 35–50% range is well calibrated, so judge these misses over many games rather than one.

suggested_change.change: Make no change. The research-backed 0.49 was the best of the estimates, and the YES result fits with a reasonable probability.

recent.question: Jaxon Smith-Njigba: 1+ touchdowns
recent.what_happened: Seattle beat the Chargers 30-23, but its touchdowns came on the ground: Emanuel Wilson scored twice and Rashid Shaheed ran one in. Smith-Njigba did not score, so his streak of games with a touchdown ended.
recent.what_we_missed: The research-backed forecast of 0.74 put too much weight on a three-game touchdown streak (6 TDs on 27 catches), which mostly reflects luck and won't keep that pace. Even elite receivers usually score in only about 45-55% of games, which is roughly the market price of 0.515. Seattle's strong running game and its lead in the game made a rushing-heavy script plausible, and that cut his scoring chances.
recent.lesson: For anytime-touchdown props, start from the player's long-run touchdown rate and the market price, and don't move far above about 55% just because of a short hot streak or headlines about records.

suggested_change.change: Cap the gap from the market on anytime-touchdown player props at about 10 points unless there is concrete news about role or injury, since recent touchdown streaks don't count as an edge.

recent.question: Will CA Mineiro win on 2026-10-03?
recent.what_happened: Atlético-MG beat Red Bull Bragantino 1-0 at Arena MRV on October 3, 2026. Bernard scored in the 17th minute. The win stretched Galo's unbeaten home run to 14 matches and took them to 43 points.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecasters went to 0.37–0.45, below the 0.505 market price, mainly because of Atlético's roughly 10 absences during the FIFA window. They gave too little weight to Atlético's strong home form (14 unbeaten at Arena MRV) and to Bragantino's own missing players and modest form. Still, a 1-0 win is a close result, and calling Yes about 50/50 was reasonable.
recent.lesson: When a team has a long unbeaten home run, don't mark them well below the market just because many players are missing; the market had probably already priced in the depleted squad.

suggested_change.change: Before moving away from the market on squad-absence news, always pull the home team's recent home record and unbeaten streak at that venue.

recent.question: King Green wins
recent.what_happened: Esteban Ribovics knocked King Green down three times and won by first-round TKO at 4:08 at UFC 332 on Oct 3, 2026 (https://bloodyelbow.com/2026/10/03/king-green-brutally-knocked-out-by-esteban-ribovics-inside-one-round-at-ufc-332/, https://www.mmamania.com/ufc-results/476672/ufc-332-results-esteban-ribovics-drops-king-green-three-times-in-wild-firefight). This ended Green's four-fight winning streak.
recent.what_we_missed: The market had Green at 36.5%, so it saw Ribovics as the clear favorite. The research-backed forecast moved up to 56% mostly because of Green's win streak and a shaky comparison of common opponents. It gave too little weight to the warning signs in its own facts: Green had just turned 40 and was fighting a 30-year-old, his weight cut was visibly hard and he swore at a cameraman, and Ribovics had just stopped Edson Barboza.
recent.lesson: When your research pushes you 20 points away from a liquid market on a fight, you need concrete new information the market doesn't have. A win streak and 'common opponents' are already priced in, and signs of a hard weight cut in a 40-year-old should lower the estimate, not raise it.

suggested_change.change: In single-fight MMA markets, cap how far the forecast can move from the market (for example, 10 points) unless the research turns up specific, verifiable news the market hasn't priced, such as an injury or a short-notice change.

recent.question: Will MrBeast Gaming's next video get between 35 and 40 million views in week 1?
recent.what_happened: The question resolved NO: MrBeast Gaming's next long-form video did not land between 35M and 40M views in its first 168 hours. My searches did not find the video's exact week-1 count.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster gave 21%, more than three times the market's 6%, for a narrow 5M-view bracket. The case rested on cumulative Tubefilter counts in the mid-40 millions and lifetime totals with unclear snapshot dates. Neither is a real week-1 figure, so there was no solid reason to put this much weight on 35–40M or to bet so heavily against the market.
recent.lesson: For narrow view-count brackets, don't stray far from the market price unless you have actual 168-hour view counts from comparable recent uploads, not cumulative or lifetime totals.

suggested_change.change: Cap how far the forecast can move from the market on narrow numeric-bracket questions when the base rate comes only from cumulative or lifetime counts rather than the metric the question resolves on.

recent.question: Will MrBeast Gaming's next video get between 30 and 35 million views in week 1?
recent.what_happened: The market most likely resolved on the September 26 upload, "I Found My 13 Year Old Minecraft World". When the forecast was made, that video was about 6.5 days into its 168-hour window and its views were apparently between 30M and 35M. That explains the 0.95 market price, and the market resolved YES. This is an inference: I didn't find an exact view count.
recent.what_we_missed: The forecaster assumed the September 26 video was "not the video this question resolves on" and forecast a future upload from base rates. A 0.95 market price six days after a new upload pointed strongly to that upload being the one in question, already inside its week-1 window and tracking in the bracket.
recent.lesson: When a view-count bracket market trades at an extreme price, first check whether the video it refers to was already posted after the market opened and is still inside its counting window. If so, look up its current views instead of using historical base rates.

suggested_change.change: For "next video" markets, record when the market was created and treat any upload after that date as the video that decides the market, rather than assuming the latest upload is excluded.

recent_wins.question: Full Game: over 55.5 points scored? (Over 55.5 points)
recent_wins.what_happened: The Chiefs beat the Raiders 30-27 on Oct 4, 2026, for a 57-point total. That cleared the 55.5 line by only 1.5 points, so the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The researched forecast (0.57) took both teams' strong 3-0 offenses seriously (KC about 29 points a game, LV 88 points scored, including a 62-point game against the Saints) and correctly dismissed the fake '24-10' snippet. Still, 55.5 looks like an alternate line well above where the main total probably sat, likely in the high 40s. The 28.5% market price was the more reasonable estimate, and the game only got over by one late field goal's worth of points, so the 0.57 call was overconfident and paid off by luck.
recent_wins.lesson: For alternate totals well above the main line, start from the market's or the main line's implied distribution, and only move far from it if you have a specific reason such as weather, injuries to the defense, or pace. Early-season points per game from three games is not enough reason on its own.

suggested_change.change: Have research pull the consensus main game total and spread, so the forecaster can see how far the question's line sits from the main total before it departs from a low market price.

recent_wins.question: Josh Allen: 1+ touchdowns
recent_wins.what_happened: Allen scored on a one-yard run with about a minute left in the second quarter against New England on Oct 4, 2026. It was his 88th career rushing/receiving touchdown, which made him the Bills' all-time leader in touchdowns from scrimmage, so the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research showed that Allen was Buffalo's main short-yardage scorer this season: 6 rushing TDs in 3 games, the latest ones on 1-yard runs. He was fully healthy, and the matchup was the league's top-scoring offense against a weak Patriots team. That justified a forecast well above the market's 0.525, which looked close to his long-run rate of scoring in about half his games. Still, even a true chance of 65–79% leaves plenty of room for a miss, and one goal-line carry decided this, so a good part of the margin was variance.
recent_wins.lesson: For QB-anytime-TD props, separate rushing from passing TDs and weight this season's goal-line role (who gets the 1-yard carries) plus the opponent's expected red-zone trips over career per-game base rates.

suggested_change.change: Pull a game-by-game log of the player's rushing TDs from last season and this one, plus his share of the team's carries inside the 5, rather than leaving the games-with-a-TD rate as 'not confirmed'.

recent_wins.question: W15 Maanshan, Qualifying: Completed Match: Yinuo Huang vs Victoria Vidal
recent_wins.what_happened: Tennis Explorer recorded the qualifying first-round match as a walkover win for Yinuo Huang on September 27. No score was played, so the match did not finish through normal play and the market resolves No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research found the 'w/o' marker on Tennis Explorer's tournament page, and Huang's profile showed no score. The rules say any walkover resolves No, which made 0.03 the right call. Without that research the forecaster said 0.77, and the market was at 0.44 even though the walkover was already public.
recent_wins.lesson: For 'completed match' markets, look up the match on live results sites like Tennis Explorer or the ITF site before forecasting, because a w/o or ret. marker settles the question right away.

suggested_change.change: For any completed-match market where the scheduled start has passed, require a results-site check for w/o or ret. markers before the forecaster falls back on base rates.

recent_wins.question: Will St. Vincent and the Grenadines win on 2026-10-03?
recent_wins.what_happened: St. Vincent and the Grenadines beat Sint Maarten 4-2 in Concacaf Nations League B Group D at FFB Stadium in Belmopán, Belize, on October 3, 2026, according to VAVEL. That is a win in regulation time, so the market resolved Yes.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research turned up current form for both teams. SVG had won both group games and had Oalex Anderson scoring regularly. Sint Maarten had lost both games without scoring and is not a FIFA member, and the match was at a neutral ground in Belize, so its nominal home edge counted for little. That moved the forecast from 0.30 without research to 0.70, above the market's 0.565. The 4-2 score shows the edge was real, not a coin flip.
recent_wins.lesson: In lower-tier Concacaf Nations League games, check recent group results, whether one side is a non-FIFA member, and whether the game is really at the home team's ground. Together these can justify backing a clear favourite above a market price that discounts it because draws count as No.

suggested_change.change: Before using any home-advantage prior, check the venue to see whether the 'home' team is actually playing at home, since many Nations League B/C games are played at a neutral site.

recent_wins.question: Mississippi St. wins
recent_wins.what_happened: No. 7 Alabama won 56-23 at No. 16 Mississippi State in Starkville on Oct 3, 2026, so the market resolved No ([Yahoo Sports](https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaaf/alabama-crimson-tide-mississippi-state-bulldogs-202610030078/), [CBS Sports](https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/gametracker/boxscore/NCAAF_20261003_BAMA@MISSST/)).
recent_wins.what_worked: Going from 0.38 without research to 0.17 with it was driven by the series history. Alabama had won 16 straight in the series (2008–2023), and from 2019 to 2023 it won by 23 to 41 points. That counted for more than Mississippi State's 4-0 start and home field. The market's 0.335 gave too much weight to the matchup of two unbeaten ranked teams.
recent_wins.lesson: When a dominant program has a long winning streak with large margins over an opponent, keep a strong lean toward the favorite even if the underdog has a hot start and a home game. Make sure the streak is current, though, because the 2024 result was taken from memory and not checked.

suggested_change.change: Get the betting spread or a computer model's win probability (for example Dimers or ESPN FPI) as an independent check, so a gap from the market like 0.17 vs 0.335 is backed by more than the series history.

recent_wins.question: Steven Fisk leads at the end of Round 2
recent_wins.what_happened: Austin Smotherman led after Round 2 with 63-62 (125), one ahead of Kevin Roy, with Kevin Streelman next. Steven Fisk was in the afternoon wave and was reported at 12-under through 8 holes of Round 2, but he did not finish in the lead, so the market resolved No.
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecaster saw that the morning players had set a very low target: Roy at -16 and finished, Streelman and Smotherman close behind. It reasoned that any afternoon player would need an exceptional finish to pass them. But none of its facts mentioned Fisk at all, so the 3% was not based on where he actually stood. He was a live threat in mid-round, which is why the market sat at 12.5%, so the result going our way was partly luck.
recent_wins.lesson: When forecasting whether a specific player will lead after a round, find that player's live score, holes left and tee wave before giving a probability. Don't infer it from the leaders alone.

suggested_change.change: For any golf leader market about a named player, require the research step to pull that player's current score and holes remaining from the live leaderboard, and flag the forecast as low-confidence if it can't.

rules.rule: For short-window crypto price questions, record a spot price from the exchange and pair named in the resolution rules (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT), no more than an hour old at judgment time when the window closes within a day, and state its timestamp and age.

For crypto threshold questions, report the percent distance from current spot to the strike, the hours left in the window, and recent realized volatility over a similar span, noting whether the window falls on a usually quieter weekend.

Read the crypto resolution rules for the exact strike, venue and test (any touch in the window or a close at a set candle), restate that strike at the top of the research, and measure every price fact against it, not against a nearby round number.

Confirm any past high or low reported as reaching the strike on the resolution venue's own candles and inside the question's window, labeling others unverified; treat earlier-week moves as background unless their driver (e.g. a bond-yield spike) is still active.

For short-horizon crypto questions, search same-day macro and geopolitical news (dollar, bond yields, oil, major policy statements) and report any specific catalyst with timestamps, or state plainly that none was found; label weeks-old news as stale background.

For single-match win questions, confirm in the rules whether only a regulation-time win counts and state that a draw resolves No; check the actual venue, since a listed home side may play at a neutral ground, and report each side's results in this competition.

For match questions, report the current-season head-to-head with its game count (under about 10 games is small; note source disagreements) and each side's dated, sourced absences and returns; when injury sources disagree, check the confirmed matchday squad or lineup.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

For tennis 'completed match' questions, read which endings count as not completed (retirement, walkover), and report the historical share of matches finished through normal play at that tour level (WTA 125, ATP Challenger) as the starting reference.

For tennis completion questions, report as risk evidence only specific, dated news from the past week: an injury, a withdrawal, or a retirement at this event; label old retirements, back-to-back events or qualifying load, and a result not yet posted as weak context.

Once a tennis match's start time has passed, check results sites (Tennis Explorer, ITF, tour site) for w/o or ret. markers first; before it, check the latest order of play and withdrawal lists, and report recent full matches each player finished.

For player touchdown props, use only facts on the named player; split rushing from receiving or passing TDs, report his share of team carries or targets inside the 5, his multi-season games-with-a-TD rate, and the team's run-pass split; label a few-game streak as small sample.

For single MMA fights, report each fighter's age, recent opponents and how those fights ended, and dated weigh-in or weight-cut news; label win streaks and common-opponent comparisons as weak evidence.

For single MLB games, report both confirmed starters' season ERA and ERA+ and recent starts, each team's season record, late-season form (record and offense since Sept 1) and home field; if it is a bullpen game, note that an opener's few innings carry little weight.

For playoff series and games, give the series score, what the trailing team still needs and where, earlier games' margins, current-season records and head-to-head, and whether standing rests on seeding; label past seasons' playoff records as small-sample background.

For in-round golf leader questions, pull the live hole-by-hole leaderboard and, for the named player and everyone within about 3 shots, report score, holes left and tee wave, plus the field's scoring average and how the rules settle a tie for the lead.

For 'next video' view questions, record when the question opened, check the channel's live upload list for any video posted since then, treat it as the resolving video, and report its upload timestamp, hours elapsed in the 168-hour window and current views.

For view-count bracket questions, build reference figures only from first-168-hour counts of the channel's recent comparable uploads; label cumulative or lifetime totals, figures with unclear snapshot dates, and months-old uploads as not the resolution metric.

When a count question resolves on one named data provider, pull that provider's own trailing 2–4 week figures and write down its counting method (e.g. AIS-visible only) first; set aside other trackers' figures that count differently.

Take historical base-rate counts and series streaks only from a cited source covering the current format and running through the latest meeting; label any count recalled from memory, disputed between sources, or built on about a dozen cases as unverified.

changes: merged R4 into R16: both cover how to treat past highs and earlier moves relative to the current window; this frees a slot under the 20-rule cap
sharpened R6 with venue and competition-form checks, because a nominal home side played at a neutral ground (polymarket:4762522)
sharpened R11 to check results sites for w/o or ret. markers first once the start time has passed, because a public walkover settled the question (polymarket:4981247)

sharpened R17 to split rushing from passing or receiving TDs, report goal-line share, multi-season TD rate and run-pass split, and treat short streaks as small samples (Allen and Smith-Njigba reviews)
added an MMA rule on age, opponent quality, weight-cut news, and treating win streaks or common-opponent comparisons as weak evidence (King Green review)

proposals.title: Claimed edge vs realised return
proposals.why: Every source is worse than the market, yet each bet claims at least 8c of edge. Bucketing settled 30c+ bets by claimed edge (8-12c, 12-20c, 20c+) and showing win rate and P&L per $100 would show whether big claimed edges are real edges or big errors. That would tell us whether to raise or lower min_edge.
proposals.judge_by: Success means Joey approves the table and it reports per-bucket P&L for each strategy. We then use it to set min_edge.

proposals.title: Claude direct, sports only
proposals.why: In sports, Claude direct scores 0.151 Brier on 67 markets against the market's 0.176 across all 232 sports markets. This is the only category where any of our sources looks better than the price. The two scores cover different sets of markets, so the comparison is suggestive only. Two-thirds of Claude's forecasts are sports, so this isolates its best area without starving the strategy of bets.
proposals.judge_by: Success means P&L per $100 staked is at least 0 and beats claude_direct's 30c+ bets over the same period. If it is below -$20 per $100 after 30 settled bets, retire it.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Retire ch3 (Claude direct, strict)
proposals.why: ch3 has placed 5 bets in 5 days and lost all 3 settled (-$60 per $100). At that pace it would take months to reach 30 results. It differs from claude_direct only by a higher edge bar and a smaller stake, so the slot is better spent on a sharper question.
proposals.judge_by: Success means the replacement challenger places more bets per day than ch3's 1 per day, so its results arrive faster.
proposals.status_reason: ch3 retired; its open bets still settle and its record stays on the page

proposals.title: Bold skips crypto, like main
proposals.why: In crypto, Jev + research scores 0.151 against the market's 0.087 over 56 resolved markets. Bold is down $20.3k, the worst of any strategy, on 33 settled. Skipping crypto leaves bold differing from main only in its info gate (0.35 vs 0.5), which makes it a clean test of that gate.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, bold's P&L per $100 staked beats its current all-time -$22 per $100, and is within $10 per $100 of main's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: bold rules v4: skips none → crypto

proposals.title: Calibrated, favourites only
proposals.why: Across strategies, bets on favourites (60c and up) have gone 12 wins to 6 losses. The calibrated forecaster went 5 for 5 there (+$3.6k), and main 2 for 2 (+$1.4k). This tests whether calibrated Jev makes money when it only backs prices of 55c and above. It is an experiment on tiny numbers.
proposals.judge_by: P&L per $100 staked is positive, and better than the calibrated strategy's over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: started automatically within the allowed bounds

proposals.title: Retire ch6 (picky Jev + research)
proposals.why: ch6 has settled 2 bets, lost both, and is down $4.0k. Its idea is to bet only where Jev disagrees with the market by 15+ points, but the market out-forecasts Jev + research (0.150 vs 0.201 Brier over 191 shared markets). Two results are noise, so this is a judgment call: the slot is better spent on a different hypothesis.
proposals.judge_by: No later check: its 3 open bets settle and are recorded, and the slot goes to the challenger below.
proposals.status_reason: ch6 retired; its open bets still settle and its record stays on the page

proposals.title: Pooled tally of bets placed under the floor
proposals.why: Each strategy has 0–1 settled bets since 2026-10-01, so the floor's '30 settled bets' test will take weeks per strategy. Pooling every strategy's 30c+ bets placed since the floor, measured against original's long shots over the same period, would answer whether the floor pays much sooner.
proposals.judge_by: The review reports pooled P&L per $100 on 30c+ bets since 2026-10-01 alongside original's under-30c bets. The floor is confirmed if the pooled result beats original's long shots.

proposals.title: Gate ledger and price breakdown for 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: The gate ledger mixes in long shots, which lost 1 in 42 before the floor. That makes every 'stopped by the info gate' number look worse than it would under today's rules: calibrated's info-stopped markets show −$7.1 per $100 (66) and main's −$24.6 (78). We can't sensibly tune the info gates until the ledger shows only markets the 30c floor would let through.
proposals.judge_by: The next reviews show a 30c+ gate ledger and a by_price_paid split for each strategy's since_change bets. It is worth having if it changes or confirms an info-gate decision once there is enough data.

proposals.title: Shrink forecasts toward the market before computing edge
proposals.why: The market's Brier (0.123, 201 markets) beats every forecaster, and most of our losses came from bets where we disagreed with it most, such as long shots that went 1 for 21. A strategy option that blends the forecast with the market price (for example 50/50) before the edge check would bet only where a disagreement survives that discount. The forecasters themselves would still never see the price.
proposals.judge_by: Replay the blended rule on resolved markets that were judged after the code ships, and compare it with the unblended rule on the same markets. It succeeds if settled P&L per $100 is higher and it has fewer losing bets.

proposals.title: Score forecasters on 30c+ markets only
proposals.why: Since 2026-10-01 every strategy bets only at 30c or more, but the Brier table (market 0.114 vs our best 0.121) mixes in the long shots we no longer touch. We need to know whether any forecaster beats the price where we actually bet, matched market by market.
proposals.judge_by: The review data gains each source's Brier score next to the market's on the same resolved markets priced 30c or more. Success means Joey can see whether any source scores below the market there, which decides which challenger to start next.

proposals.title: Paired Brier scores and a calibration sanity check
proposals.why: Each source is scored on a different set of markets (Claude on 33, the market on 120), so 'Claude beats the market' can't be trusted. The calibration map has a=1.489, and its forecasts score worse than raw Jev (0.236 against 0.199), even though reviews blame Jev being overconfident. A=1.489 may be stretching forecasts further from 50/50 instead of pulling them back.
proposals.judge_by: Joey approves, and the next review shows Brier scores for each source against the market on the same resolved markets, plus the calibrated source's score on markets the map wasn't fitted to.
proposals.status_reason: approved by Joey 2026-10-02; needs a code session

This tests whether requiring a 15% edge, and dropping both categories, turns research-driven bets profitable. It can run now, while main is locked until tomorrow.

proposals.title: Jev alone, bold: pickier, no crypto or economy
proposals.why: Jev alone scores worse than the market in every category, with a Brier of 0.221 against 0.052 in crypto (21 resolved) and 0.294 against 0.168 in economy (12 resolved). This strategy has lost $17 per $100 staked (22 bets, 6 settled). The experiment is to demand a bigger edge and skip Jev's worst categories, while leaving the info gate at 0.2 so it stays distinct from Jev alone.
proposals.judge_by: On bets opened after this change, P&L per $100 staked beats its all-time -$17.4 per $100 and is at least as good as jev_alone over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: jev_alone_bold rules v2: edge bar 8% → 12%; skips none → crypto, economy

proposals.title: Break results down by price paid
proposals.why: Many losses, including all 3 of claude_direct's and every info-gate-stopped group, show -$100 per $100, meaning the whole stake was lost. That pattern suggests we may be buying cheap longshots. A breakdown of wins and P&L by ask price (for example <0.2, 0.2–0.5, 0.5–0.8, >0.8), for placed and stopped bets, would let us set min_ask and max_ask from evidence instead of guessing.
proposals.judge_by: The review data includes a by-price breakdown, and within 2 reviews it leads to either a min_ask/max_ask tune or a clear finding that price doesn't matter.

proposals.title: Claude direct, pickier and without crypto
proposals.why: Claude is our best forecaster (Brier 0.132 on 24) yet lost all 3 of its settled bets. The places where it disagrees with the market by only 8% are probably where the market is right. This challenger demands a 12% edge, skips crypto, and bets half as much per bet.
proposals.judge_by: Positive P&L, and more P&L per $100 staked than claude_direct over the same period.
proposals.status_reason: retired by the daily review 2026-10-04: ch3 has placed 5 bets in 5 days and lost all 3 settled (-$60 per $100). At that pace it would take months to reach 30 results. It differs from claude_direct only by a higher edge bar and a smaller sta

proposals.title: Bold meets the info gate halfway
proposals.why: Bold's extra bets, where Jev's info rating is 0.2–0.5, are losing $31.79 per $100 (7 bets), and main's info-stopped markets lose $70 per $100 (16). A 0.35 threshold tests where the cutoff really belongs, without collapsing bold into a copy of main.
proposals.judge_by: Bold's P&L per $100 staked since the change beats its old -$31.79 per $100, and is closer to or above main's over the same period.

proposals.title: Main skips crypto
proposals.why: In crypto the market scores a Brier of 0.034 against Jev+research's 0.117 (9 resolved), so any edge we think we see there is most likely our own error. This is an experiment on a small sample.
proposals.judge_by: On the yardstick, main's P&L on bets opened after this change is at least original's. Meanwhile, original's crypto bets over the same period lose money in total.
proposals.status_reason: main rules v2: skips none → crypto

retro.headline: A quiet half-day with only a dozen resolved bets under the new 30c floor across all strategies, too few to judge it; the market price still out-forecasts every source we have, so I'm swapping a near-dormant challenger for a sharper test of our best forecaster.
went_well: Calibrated is the least-bad strategy all time: -$6.8k on 12 settled, or -$17 per $100 staked against -$25 for main. Its favourites (60c and up) are 5 for 5 for +$3.6k. That is only 5 bets, so it's a hint, not a finding.
The 30c floor looks right in hindsight. In every strategy's history, long shots under 30c won 1 of 59 settled bets and lost about $87.4k. Since the floor went in on 10-01, no strategy has placed one.
Jev alone, bold's only settled bet since its tune won +$2.7k, and main is 2-2 since the floor. These are 1 and 4 results, which is noise.
went_badly: Nobody beats the market price. Across 255 markets that every source forecast, the market scores 0.146 Brier, Claude direct 0.179, Jev + research 0.205 and Jev alone 0.249 (lower is better). Every strategy is down: main -$12.2k, bold -$24.7k.

The yardstick doesn't yet show that tuning main pays. On shared bets since 09-29, main lost $8,951 on $35.5k staked (-$25 per $100) and original lost $10,042 on $46.6k (-$22 per $100). Those rest on 12 and 17 settled bets, so neither is better yet.

Claude direct is our best forecaster, but its bets lose: 1 win in 8 settled, -$52 per $100. Its stricter challenger ch3 is 0 for 3 (-$3.0k) and has placed only 5 bets in 5 days, so it will never gather enough data.
